combined_coverage: Use examples/terraform-analytics/coverage.json for every assigned provider resource/data-source pair. The types below replace that fixture's none/unexercised annotations for this second workflow. Neither file is lifecycle evidence by itself.
requirements: Build the current stackd binary before the integration owner runs the fixture.
Use Python 3.11 or newer, Terraform 1.15.9, host psql, and an available Docker daemon.
Install every pinned image below. Missing images and failed actual consumers are errors, not skipped stages.

Read compute/glue/AWS-GLUE-LICENSE.txt and the repository license boundary. This workflow develops and verifies an AWS-targeted Glue application. It does not redistribute the images or establish a generic other-cloud Spark runtime.

The fixture uses the shared examples/local.py safety, environment, client, workspace, and controller functions. It creates a unique controller database, bucket, names, native PostgreSQL container, and native Kafka namespaces.

The provider requests the STS account. S3 and S3Control endpoints are explicit. The verified existing HTTP proxy admission pattern routes the SDK's signed account-prefixed S3Control host through this same owned listener. No DNS/hosts mutation, provider fork, or external forwarding is used.
Sensitive tfstate, input password, access-key outputs, and import snapshots remain in the private owned workspace. The committed fixture has no credentials. The report does not record secrets.
actual_consumers: A Glue 5.0/G.1X/two-worker Spark container reads this workflow's run properties and cataloged Hive UDF class. Spark loads and executes that class. It is explicit application consumption of a Glue UDF definition, not automatic Athena or Spark Glue-catalog UDF resolution.

The actual Spark Hadoop S3A writer writes partitioned CSV objects with the selected security configuration. Independent signed S3 reads check the real bytes and SSE-KMS key in revision 1, and SSE-S3 in revision 2.

A conditional workflow trigger admits the S3 and PostgreSQL crawlers only after the actual Spark job succeeds. The S3 crawler uses the Terraform CSV classifier and actual objects to produce a partitioned table. Trino reads both that discovered table and the separately managed indexed table. SDK and S3 consumers compare paginated rows and actual query-result objects.

A separate native PostgreSQL database contains real rows and a changed native schema. A Secrets Manager-backed Terraform Glue connection feeds the actual PostgreSQL crawler. A second libpq process authenticates with the same credentials and independently reads the real rows. The fixture checks the discovered columns and the configured exclusion.

The selected Glue password setting encrypts an ephemeral ordinary connection with real KMS. An independent KMS Decrypt verifies its secret under the connection ARN context. After the Terraform setting update, the normal connection read decrypts the existing ciphertext. HidePassword redacts both projections.

An independent fastavro producer serializes with the actual registry schema version and AWS's published uncompressed schema-version header. Native Kinesis stores the bytes. A separate Kinesis and Glue consumer resolves the received version UUID and deserializes the real payload. Revision 2's compatible reader also reads revision 1's payload.

Kinesis account commitment is enabled, then disabled before its earliest end. The fixture checks the actual deferred status, actual ON_DEMAND native Kafka topology, four-to-five warm-throughput shards, and real records. It does not claim paid managed capacity or an AWS throughput SLA.

An independent signed IAM reader has identity allows. The current Glue resource-policy deny overrides one allow, and a mutable policy update changes which actual read is denied. Root Terraform reads are not suppressed or redirected.

Controller reopen must retain the actual Spark marker, completed workflow and prior Avro record bytes. Fresh Spark/UDF, S3/Trino, PostgreSQL/libpq, KMS/password, schema-record and current-policy consumers run again.

Declared-apply reconciliation admits observed null-to-empty collections and exact separately managed IAM policy or Glue partition-index projections. The catalog table is read before its ForceNew index replacement completes, so the same bounded check runs after revision 2 apply. Strict refresh-only exit 2 is retained only when the exact plan JSON has no resource drift, resource changes or changed output actions. Independent consumers and ordinary destroy still run, but final status remains failed. Neither nonzero no-op nor semantic drift is accepted.

types.remainder: Root-catalog metadata and actual crawler consumers are included. Resource links, federation, and Lake Formation default grants are not exercised here.
Actual partitioned CSV Trino reads are included. Governed transactions, multi-dialect views, managed Iceberg creation/update, and transactional snapshots are unavailable or unexercised.

CSV delimiter mutation is consumed by actual discovery. JSON/XML/Grok classifiers, custom datatype controls, alternate serde/quote/header/trimming modes and classifier-type replacement are not exercised by this fixture.

Real PostgreSQL JDBC and Secrets Manager credential consumption are included. PASSWORD in Terraform combined with ReturnConnectionPasswordEncrypted=true changes the returned property to ENCRYPTED_PASSWORD; this does not establish provider-state convergence for that configuration. The fixture uses SECRET_ID for the managed connection and an independent password consumer. Authentication v2/OAuth/custom auth, generic JDBC, VPC, and create-time credential validation remain unavailable or unexercised.

Actual S3 CSV and native PostgreSQL discovery run in the real workflow and update from real source bytes/schema. Incremental/event/lineage/Lake Formation/federated/other JDBC discovery, VPC, and managed DPU accounting are not established.
Real connection-password KMS projections and default-disabled destroy reset are included. Entire-catalog/Lake Formation KMS encryption is explicitly rejected, not retained as enabled metadata.

Required actual Glue 5.0/G.1X/two-worker Spark job, description/default-argument/security update and native UDF/S3 execution are included. The first fixture separately has optional Python-shell 3.9 execution. Other versions/capacities/workers, FLEX, Ray/streaming, bookmarks, extra modules/JARs/files, connections flags, runtime selection, queuing and source-control/maintenance/notification settings remain unavailable or unexercised.
Both actual CSV partition consumers and descriptor/parameter updates are included. Other formats and transactional snapshots are not established.
Create/import/ForceNew key-name update/refresh/destroy and an independent partition-expression consumer are included. Metadata lifecycle is not a native index-acceleration or performance claim.
ARN import, mutable description/tags, real schema and native-record consumers are included. Cross-account, additional formats, and all quota/status cases are not exercised.
Region singleton import and actual signed identity-allow/resource-deny mutation are included. Cross-account grants and hybrid Lake Formation modes are not exercised.

AVRO BACKWARD int-to-long evolution, ARN import, real native-record serialization/deserialization, and prior-version reader resolution are included. JSON/Protobuf and all compatibility/checkpoint/error/status/version-deletion cases are not exercised.

Name import, ForceNew replacement, and actual Spark S3 SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 bytes are included. CloudWatch encryption, bookmark encryption, data-quality encryption/execution and external dependency consumers are not established.

Explicit on-demand workflow start and activated conditional job-success actions execute real job/crawlers. Scheduled/event modes, disabled/revoked/failure/retry/concurrency races and all predicates remain unexercised.

Native Spark executes the actual cataloged installed Hive UDF class, then executes its mutable replacement class. Automatic Athena/Spark catalog resolution and external resource-URI/JAR installation are not established.
Real job/crawler graph, default-run-property mutation and actual consumers are included. Scheduled roots, all stop/resume/retry/concurrency/authority-failure modes remain unexercised.

Reads a real tagged plain child catalog created and cleaned by the independent SDK prerequisite. The pinned Terraform catalog RESOURCE requires modes rejected by this owner; this data-source read does not establish that resource's support.
Actual name-based registry read is included. Foreign/denied/missing-region behavior is not exercised.
Actual CSV indexed-table metadata is included. Time-travel/transaction views are unexercised.
Actual current Secrets Manager-backed connection read is included. Terraform encrypted-PASSWORD state convergence is not established.
Reads actual password configuration in both revisions. Whole-catalog encryption is unavailable.

Region import, ENABLED-to-deferred-DISABLED update, refresh and real warm-topology/record consumers are included. The pinned provider has no-op Delete; the fixture explicitly checks retained commitment, not fictitious removal. The full 24-hour expiry and paid managed capacity/SLA are not exercised.

Actual ON_DEMAND and warm-throughput four-to-five native topology/Avro records are included. The first fixture covers PROVISIONED. Encryption, large-record/rate-limit/retention-expiry behavior and all topology edge cases are not exercised.

Actual engine-3 reads consume crawler and indexed CSV tables. First fixture covers native partitioned CTAS/INSERT/manifests. Spark Athena, managed results, capacity and other unsupported configurations are not admitted as metadata-only support.

absent_provider_families.reason: Capacity APIs and real reserved capacity are unavailable.
Pinned resource requires federation, Redshift or managed data-lake catalog properties. Those control/data planes are unavailable. Plain SDK catalogs do not satisfy it.
Required optimizer lifecycle APIs and actual Iceberg optimization are unavailable.
Required ruleset lifecycle APIs and actual quality execution are unavailable.
Required development endpoint APIs and actual compute/networking are unavailable.
Required ML lifecycle APIs and actual transform runtime are unavailable.
CreateScript native code generation is unavailable.

other_cohort_types: Athena catalog/database/named/prepared queries, Kinesis consumer/resource policy/data sources, and Firehose resource/data source are enumerated and have their runnable consumers in examples/terraform-analytics. Their exact remaining settings are retained in its coverage.json. Neither successful fixture would alone establish every current provider setting.
change_notes: Firehose admits ordinary disabled format-conversion and dynamic-partitioning configuration blocks emitted by the current provider. It preserves inactive format/retry details on mutable destination updates. Enabled format conversion, implicit-enabled format conversion, and enabled dynamic partitioning remain explicitly unavailable.

Glue PutDataCatalogEncryptionSettings replaces password settings. An empty provider delete restores default-disabled password state and clears stale key references without changing CloudFormation ownership. Enabled whole-catalog encryption remains explicitly unavailable.

Native Athena database drops use Spark's typed namespace AST. A Glue-owned atomic RESTRICT check and metadata cascade preserve public DeleteDatabase semantics, current IAM, and real S3 bytes. The first fixture includes the required native SQL/S3 regression.

Both fixtures inspect the post-create refresh projection for known null-to-empty collections and exact separately managed IAM policies or Glue indexes. Catalog revision 2 also checks the exact new index after its declared ForceNew replacement. No remote mutation, arbitrary drift acceptance, or ignore_changes is allowed. Later refresh/no-op stages remain strict.

Both job fixtures declare STANDARD execution class. The pinned provider reads that real default into an optional, non-computed field; an omitted declaration produces an ordinary update plan. The native job mode is unchanged.
PostgreSQL readiness uses TCP. The image's temporary socket-only initdb server is not sufficient readiness. Failed native SQL retains its actual stderr in the private workspace.

Partial catalog cleanup disables an enabled owned Kinesis billing commitment with the declared Terraform account-settings resource before ordinary destroy. The real early-disable deadline remains; the provider's absent Delete is not invented.
Both fixtures reopen the same owned SQLite database and repeat real consumers. Strict core refresh failures retain exact plans and fail the final run after cleanup.
Recent native Hive write manifests and calibrated Glue absent-statistics deletion are unchanged.
